data.narrative:
Rainmaker operates in the Drones & Autonomous sector at Series A stage, having raised $25M to date. The comparable universe includes 8 private firms in the sector (Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, Elroy Air among them) and no public peers, limiting direct benchmarking options.

Only one valuation method proved applicable. Stage-Progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy baseline of $25M and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, yields an implied valuation of $50M. Peer-Median methodology could not be applied: while 5 same-sector peers exist, insufficient depth in same-stage or adjacent-stage comparable cohorts (fewer than the required 3 datapoints) precluded reliable median extraction without risking distortion from broader-sector anchoring.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $42M to $57M, with a median point of $50M. This single-method result carries material uncertainty given reliance on stage-progression mechanics alone and absence of peer-derived cross-checks. Key risks to valuation include the nascency of comparable datasets in autonomous systems (especially at Series A) and dependency on the appropriateness of the 2.0x multiplier for this sector's capital progression patterns. Additional clarity on Rainmaker's revenue, unit economics, or technology differentiation relative to named peers would strengthen conviction in this range.
